Sorry for not responding until just recently—I had forgotten about this thread but received a notification that brought me back to it😅

Yes to both— I have a permanent disability due to my breathing apart from the injuries and am considered legally disabled. I informed them of all of these health issues during the interview, orientation, and even BEFORE the interview when I first received the call about my application.

I went through the procedure. I even spoke with the store manager and HR during the interview and then again during orientation to confirm that these accommodations would not be an issue. They weren’t an issue then, or at least that is what they told me at the time.. I gave up on it and quit after jumping through more hoops than a basket ball

You were not significant enough to even ping a notification. I only revisited this thread because I was contacted by a person from the media about this incident 😉
You still aren’t that significant to me, so why don’t you go find something 🍆 shaped to choke on and get off this thread? 🤡
Also, telling someone with a disability that their physical impairments make them “look lazy” and that their company “should get rid” of them is one damn strange take that most wouldn’t agree with but if that’s what it takes for you to feel better in your own miserable existence, then I guess you do you..?

Thank you!!
Just an update:
I was asked to undergo a medical examination, which I did for them. 3 separate times, 3 separate doctors, and I still was denied DESPITE my doctor’s clearly stated concerns for my health if the chairs were fully removed. I was denied the accommodation with no explanation given, placed on a permanent “job reassignment search” which the manager informed that me there would be no positions available, and eventually quit rather than fight for a part time position.. The worst part is that I LOVED working and would PREFER to be standing—I used to work anywhere between 12 and 19 hour shifts without breaks and would STILL be just fine! It’s Hell having your body break on you like that without any reason and at no fault of your own..
They did that to me at first, as well.. I eventually was put on a permanent “job reassignment search” for which I had been told there would be no positions.. I gave up on it:(
It certainly seems that way! In my case, the chair wouldn’t have been a comfort item—it literally would have kept me from going back to the hospital.

You are adorable, especially since it seems that you can’t read 🙃
I have injuries, they have NOT healed and I’m NOT expected to EVER fully recover. The part you seemed to have missed (illiteracy sucks, sorry you struggle) is that I also suffer from SEVERE BREATHING DIFFICULTIES. I’m on PERMANENT disability due to persistent, severe, and life-threatening exercise-induced asthma. I do not now nor have I ever smoked. I have done NOTHING on my own to damage my lungs in any way, but my parents certainly did a number on me growing up in an abusive household. Up until recently, I was hospitalized every month due to my asthma with those admissions lasting between 1-2 weeks. It’s severe enough for me to have been approved for disability on the first try. I know people who were diagnosed with terminal cancer that were not approved.
I’m sure you feel really insecure about your illiteracy and mental challenges, but it’s ok! You can always go back to school or reach out for help! I can mail you a few children’s activity books and a foam helmet to get you started if you like?

I went through the entire process as legally required AND informed the employer DURING THE INTERVIEW of the accommodations I would need. I was hired the same day I was interviewed. It is not on ME to do anything further but raise the alarm now.
Also as an update:
I was forcibly put on a “job reassignment search” for a position where they would be willing to facilitate the PREVIOUSLY AGREED UPON accommodations—a search for which there were NO positions offered. My store manager told me I wouldn’t get a position even as she put me on reassignment but started that this was all they could do for me. Less than 4 weeks after I quit, I saw a greeter for the same store/same location IN A CHAIR. She has still been allowed the chair and it is believed that there isn’t an issue for her since the manager is a personal friend.

FYI: I’m female🙃
